utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we please have appearances for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, counsel. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. Mark Harmon and Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. On behalf of Mr. Perisic today, Tina Drolec, Alex Fielding and Novak Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning to you, Mr. Kovacevic. Just to remind you that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kovacevic. Before I pick up where I left off yesterday, and we were talking about fuel, there is an additional question I would like to ask you in relation to something that we were talking about yesterday. You were answering questions yesterday in relation to the personnel structure of the VRS. You explained that some of the officers and NCOs of the VRS were actually the former active-duty JNA officers who grew up around those parts and who were now joining this new army. You remember talking about that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have any information at the time as to what became of active-duty members of the JNA before the war, Croats, Macedonians, Slovenians, Muslims, were they now joining these newly established armies such as these men that we referred to awhile ago were now joining the VRS?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know is that as early as during the actual clashes between the JNA and the armed forces in Croatia, there was an interstate agreement allowing for the possibility that the Croats, ethnic Croats, who were then in Croatian territory were entitled to draw their pension from the then-Yugoslavia, which at that point was still the SFRY, and draw their pension from the JNA, regardless of whether they were in fact members of the JNA or whether for a brief while perhaps they were members of the Croatian army. Something similar occurred in May 1992, when the decision was taken for the JNA to withdraw from Bosnia and Herzegovina. Ethnic Croats and Muslims, or at least those who were for awhile with the HVO or the armies of the BH TO could now --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Perhaps we are talking at cross-purposes here. I'm not talking about pension. I'm talking about something else. Do you know who made up the body of officers of the BH army and the HVO and the Croatian army? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The members of the former JNA, those who were ethnic Croats and Muslims, were able to join the VA. It was certainly like that. Members of the BH army, on the other hand, were for the most part ethnic Muslims, or ethnic Croats. There were Serbs among them too, not so many though. More or less the same situation applied in the HVO, the Croats' army. Even in the VRS later on there remained a number of ethnic Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't think you've answered my question fully.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who -- who -- which kinds of officer made up the BH army? Where did they hail from in terms of status? Were they former civilians or perhaps coming from another body or army? If you know, please answer.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the first men who were there who -- first leaders of the BH army were members of the former JNA. Former members of the former JNA. Some of them I knew personally. Rasim Delic, Colonel Vehbija Karic and others as well. There were, nevertheless, quite a number, especially of brigade commanders, who were former civilians or people from the TO, the kind of men then referred to as self-styled brigade commanders, such as Juka Prazina and Celo, as well as others.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, I would like to go back now to the topic that we discussed yesterday, fuel and fuel supplies to the VRS during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have the following document drawn up: It's a 65 ter document, Defence document, 00761D. Wrong document, I see the B/C/S. I'll just repeat, maybe it wasn't -- just a minute. Just a second. Again, 65 ter Defence document 00761D. We do have that document on our screens. That's it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have a look, sir. This is self-explanatory. I will have a question about something in particular, a single sentence, General. This is a document from the Drina Corps Command. It was dispatched to all the Drina Corps units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please pull this up a little so the General can see the bottom of this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, I would like you to comment on a particular sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's right under that lengthy paragraph which I'm about to read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The assistant logistics commander of the Drina Corps says: "In conversation with these individuals, they claim to be able to supply fuel and that they are doing too. Nevertheless, no command has reported to their staff about any quantities received. The logical conclusion is that some units even have a surplus of fuel." General, this is the summer of 1993, you were at the time defence minister. What did you know about the fuel supplies in certain units in the VRS and the supply levels?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct. It tallies with what I knew at the time, namely that the units had sufficient supply levels of fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a number for this document, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D411. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who in the VRS made decisions regarding the distribution of such fuel as was made available to the VRS? At what level was that decision taken and how?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the commodity reserves of the RS for the most part stored any fuel obtained also for the purposes of the army. They would then inform the Main Staff, the defence ministry, as well as the government that there was a certain commodity reserves depot where a certain amount of fuel could be found that was to be used for the army's purposes. Under the regulations that prevailed, it was the Main Staff alone who could decide on the distribution of fuel to all of its subordinate units and this is something that they did. They would then inform units or send orders to the corps saying that a certain amount of fuel was allocated to them that was there to be picked up from one of the depots, and they were now free to use it for their own ends.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another 65 ter document, Defence document, 00832D. As for the previous document -- all right, I apologise. I apologise, this is not the right document. Can I have a minute, please. It's not about this topic. Just to see whether we can do it while it's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is not just about the topic that we discussed, namely fuel. The document talks about something else that we mentioned earlier on. General, can you please comment on this. Who is this delivered to; who is dispatching this document to whom; and what is this procedure about?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is about the following procedure: The Main Staff draws up a distribution list for mines produced for the army's purposes. Other kinds of equipment are also involved specifically from the Elektromechanika Enterprise where they produced 1.260 impact rifle grenades. The Main Staff is now to draw up a distribution chart and specify the units to be allocated ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have a small discrepancy in the heading of the document. General, who is this delivered to? What is KM and PKM, what does that stand for?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reads "Delivered to," and I will give you the full title: "The Main Staff of the VRS command post, rear command post."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, Your Honours, the discrepancy is what we find in parentheses there in the English, but I think the General has now sufficiently clarified this. "PKM" means "rear command post." For my purposes we could admit this document into evidence without requesting a retranslation of the entire document just because of this single discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The matter has been corrected on the record. I'm satisfied with that correction and I have no objection to its admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Let the Chamber be clarified. This document is from the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska Army, strictly confidential number that, of 26 of September. It is to be delivered to the General Staff of the VRS of Republika -- rear command post. Now, what I would like to understand is where physically is the rear command post in relation to the main office of the Main Staff of the army?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you remember, Your Honours, General Skrbic testified to that. I could ask General Kovacevic the same question, nevertheless.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, in relation to the location -- or rather, first of all, tell us where was the Main Staff of the VRS located, and then tell us where the rear command post was located?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VRS Main Staff was located at Crna Rijeka. The distance between Han Pijesak and Crna Rijeka being about 5 to 6 kilometres. It was in the middle of the woods. The facility was built and equipped during the time of the former JNA. There were a number of huts there, as well as an underground facility to be used in the eventuality of a nuclear war. At Crna Rijeka and in those huts, General Mladic, General Milovanovic, and General Gvero were often to be found, as well as other security officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The rear command post --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just tell us where the rear command post was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Crna Rijeka, next to Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So the Main Staff was in Crna Rijeka. The rear command post was in Crna Rijeka, next to Han Pijesak. That's the answer. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we had an interpretation issue now. Let me repeat what His Honour just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where was the rear command post?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the centre of the town of Han Pijesak in Hotel Planinka, a civilian hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D412. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up Defence document from the 65 ter list 00831D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to the issue of fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to apologise to Mr. Harmon. I'm told by my colleague that we omitted to place this document on the list because it's 00832 and 00831 was placed on the list. So if Mr. Harmon has an objection to that, I will withdraw the document, but it was a typo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I can have just a minute to look at the document, Your Honour. We can proceed, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just briefly, please. We discussed this already when you said who made decisions on how to distribute fuel, so just look at the document and tell us if it's consistent with what you've just been telling us?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this document speaks to the fact that the Chief of the Main Staff of the VRS, General Milovanovic, distributed the stated amount of fuel and ordered that the said amount be set aside for the purposes of this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify one issue, General. There is an acronym here which was not translated. Where it says "order RDRR," what does this stand for? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commodity reserves, or rather, war-time state commodity reserves.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Has that got anything to do with the directorate you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the reserves were under the sole authority of the directorate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D413. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will move to a different topic now, General. We will go back to the issue we broached yesterday but we'll now speak specifically of, and that's the budget of the Republika Srpska and specifically the budget line for the VRS. I will make a distinction between the period up until the end of 1993 and the subsequent period. What were the basic sources of revenue for the RS budget up until the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the source of budget revenue was customs, various other types of revenue as envisaged under the law. However, most of the revenue originated from the loans granted by the National Bank of Republika Srpska which covered the budget, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the course of 1993 the loans were in fact also funded by the FRY?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that the RS National Bank also took loans from the FRY National Bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did this continue in 1994 and onwards?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, especially not when sanctions were imposed and when a new tender, the new dinar was introduced in the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We heard evidence here that in early January of 1994, the so-called economic programme of the new FRY government was pursued and these were, in fact, specifically Mr. Avramovic's economic and financial policy. So has this got anything to do with the loans coming from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, it was impossible to obtain loans. I know that decisions were taken to secure additional sources of revenue to the budget by selling --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm interrupting you there, but just tell us in what sentence what the gist of the programme of Governor Avramovic was with regard to the stability of the dinar? What changed? What was there before and what changed afterwards?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the gist of the policy was to cut the spending and to separate the financial obligations of Republika Srpska from those of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was hyperinflation curbed through these measures?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the money printing from the primary emission put a stop to in this way?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From the beginning of 1994 onwards, what were the sources of budgetary revenue in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tax collection, customs revenue, various levies, taxes levied on Republika Srpska citizens employed abroad which revenue was collected indirectly, then the sale of various goods and capitals present in Republika Srpska, and loans from the RS National Bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the budget itself sufficient for the needs of and requirements of the army?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The budget was not sufficient to cover all the needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps this question could be clarified as to time because it would be more helpful to everybody if we knew the time when we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything that we will now be discussing is the period from the beginning of 1994 when new economic programmes were introduced in the FRY onwards. And I'm interested in knowing how the army was financed from the budget and outside of the budget at the time when the so-called sound or solid dinar was introduced up until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Then perhaps a foundation could be laid, Your Honour, because this witness stopped being the minister of defence at a certain point in time, and I think if we're going to have a broad expansive inquiry into the sufficiency of the budget, then a foundation has to be laid as to how this witness knows about the budget after he ceased being minister of defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it would also be helpful for the Chamber to know when the solid dinar was introduced.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the Torkildsen spoke to this, if I recall. But I don't want to testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, can you tell us if you remember, when was Avramovic's dinar introduced, as it were, or in fact the convertible dinar, when was it introduced in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a precise figure to give you, but I know that from the start of 1994, through to the end of my term of office, at my proposal, at the proposal of the Supreme Command and at the proposal of the government, the National Assembly of Republika Srpska carried two laws.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us first deal with the objection by Mr. Harmon. So you don't know the exact date when the new dinar was introduced. Let's move on from there, then. My next question, up until what time were you defence minister? I think you said it on the first day.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was roughly until the month of August of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which position did you take up subsequently?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For awhile I was deputy defence minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Up until when was that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the way to the period when I was -- I became eligible for retirement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said this, I think, on the first day to Their Honours, but can you repeat it, when was this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was six months before my actual date of retirement and you will find the date, the exact date, in my personnel file.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I put to you that it was June 1995 since you were retired in January of 1996; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During your term in office as deputy defence minister, were you privy to the information in possession of the government and defence ministry about the budgetary funds and non-budgetary funds that were made available to the army?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was privy to that based on two sources. One was the ministry itself, and the other was the state committee for centralised procurement for the purposes of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Lukic, I thought you said at page 13, line 13: "I put it to you that it was June 1995 since you were retired in January 1996; is that right?" I see the transcript says "2006," so I just want to make sure that that is corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you were right in noticing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So can you tell us again which year were you retired?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Of course. That's all I wanted to correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mentioned this committee, which I can't repeat its title correctly, you'll tell us, but tell us, please, when was this committee formed, who composed it and what did it do?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. I think it was in mid-1995. The committee was composed of quite a few people. It was headed by the then-president, Radovan Karadzic. There was General Mladic as well as the prime minister. I know that it was decided that I should be the secretary of this state committee for centralised procurement for the armed forces of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the basic role of the committee? Tell us in a sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The procurement of all manner of goods was to be conducted in a centralised manner in one place, that's to say, this committee headed by Radovan Karadzic and within presence of General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the witness has shown with his answers that he is capable of telling us how the army was financed, through what means, in 1994 and 1995. I can see Mr. Harmon nodding. So I would like to proceed with this line of questioning then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we get your nod on the record, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm satisfied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that, according to what you knew at the time, the budget was not sufficient, not sufficient in order to make sure sufficient funds were available to the army. You said the other day that the needs expressed by Republika Srpska were one thing, but the actual allocation is a different thing altogether, needs being expressed by the VRS in relation to its real needs. What happened with these in that period and throughout 1995? Were their needs realistic or exaggerated?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my experience, the way they expressed their needs was somewhat exaggerated in relation to what was actually necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. And I note that we started late but it's the time for break. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the record, Mr. Guy-Smith and our intern, Oonagh O'Connor, are here with us for the following session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, we are back in open session and I would like to pick up where we left off before the break about extra budgetary funds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have Defence 65 ter document 00830D. Could we please pull this up a little so the General can see the date and who signed the document. To the left, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, are you familiar with this document? If so, what can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with it. It's a government decision on procuring supplies of all derivatives to be included in the commodity reserves. The Ministry of Trade is hereby put in charge of implementing this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 2 talks about funds, the funds for the payment of this amount, 4.600.000 German marks will be secured by taking out a loan with the National Bank of Republika Srpska. Is that in keeping with what you said before? What about this loan for this particular job, is that something that comes from the budget or is this an extra budgetary transaction being bankrolled by the National Bank of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is extra budgetary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have a number for this document, please, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the document be given a number and admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D414. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another document that I'd like to show the witness while we are still on this topic, 65 ter Defence list 00722D -- rather, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 00722D. Defence ministry document, the 25th of November, 1993, delivered to the Main Staff -- or rather, addressed to the Main Staff of the VRS. Can we have page 3 in the B/C/S, please, showing who authored the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see a stamp there and the signature of the assistant commander for moral guidance and religious affairs. I suppose he worked in a particular unit, but that's not what I want to know about. Right above where it says there, General, do you know who produced this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that this comes from the defence ministry but I'm not familiar with the document's substance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll be reading back to you a number of different paragraphs just to make sure whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you do that. Sir, you say you believe it comes from the defence ministry but you are not familiar with the document. Do you by any chance know who the defence minister Dusan Kovacevic is who is written at the bottom of that document as one of the co-signatories?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you remember you authoring this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm confused by one thing, the document says the accuracy of the transcript is hereby certified by assistant commander Colonel Vukelic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then the corps seal. Or the corps stamp. I find that confusing. That is precisely why I said I would like to be given an opportunity to familiarise myself with the substance of this document. Once I've done that, I could perhaps give you more informed opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It would be helpful that you do familiarise yourself with the document and tell us whether indeed you are the co-author of the document. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We went through this document during our proofing perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Give the witness an opportunity to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go to page 1 of this document. It numbers three pages in total. And perhaps we should give the General a chance to read some of this, have a look to see for himself. Maybe that will jog his memory. Could we pull it up, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, now that you've had a look, do you remember anything in connection with this document? Were you involved in the production of this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this document was produced in the defence ministry. Everything stated here is accurate in terms of the document's substance. I am one of the signatories jointly with Mr. Lukic, the president of the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to elicit several comments from you because a number of different topics are mentioned here. Perhaps you can shed some light on some of these, specifically government decisions. Paragraph 1, a little lower down page 1 where it reads: "At the 84th session of the government."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you can see that too, I hope?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The government adopted a decree imposing the obligation of the municipalities and enterprise to provide and distribute to the army personnel and so on and so forth, in the reserve force. Do you remember whether that decree was in fact adopted and did it get ever off the ground, in a manner of speaking?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that decree was adopted and it was about compensating members of the army, soldiers in lieu of salaries, financial compensation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have page 2 now, please, both English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to have your comment on paragraph 5, which is where you state: "For the next session of the People's Assembly of the VRS, the government has proposed a bill on loans to be used to finance the VRS. If the bill is passed, its implementation will start by the 1st of December, 1993." Do you remember whether the bill was actually passed by the Assembly, and would that loan be within the framework of the budget or an extra budgetary loan in terms of funding the VRS?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I was one of the people who were involved in drafting this bill. The bill was then reviewed at a government meeting, certain amendments were made and the bill was then duly adopted. It was submitted to the People's Assembly of the RS, after which a final document was adopted and published in the "Official Gazette" of the RS. It then took effect, but the results were not those expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 7 of this document: "The government adopted a conclusion that 10 per cent of the income in the timber and wood processing industry would be allocated on a monthly basis to fund the army." Do you remember if that conclusion was adopted and were any steps taken in accordance with that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this conclusion and it was adopted by the RS government. The conclusion was forwarded to the management of the RS forestry which was the central state company in charge of the country's woodlands. The conclusion orders the company to put aside 10 per cent of its overall proceeds in the sales of timber and earmark those funds to be used by the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could I have a number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D415. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have a look at an OTP exhibit and that is P1534. It addresses an issue that we have been discussing. Can we also have the left-hand side of the document in the B/C/S zoomed in. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have before us the report on the work of the defence ministry for the period between August 1994 and November 1995. Are you familiar with this document, General?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will skip the introductory remarks, and tell us first who the report was addressed to and what were the sources that was based on?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report was addressed to the government of Republika Srpska, the Main Staff of the VRS, the president of Republika Srpska, the office of the speaker of the parliament, that's to say, the president of the National Assembly, and specific ministers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we turn to page 3 in B/C/S and 5 in English. This is the portion entitled "Military Economy" -- "Military Industry."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The report reads: "The Ministry of Defence focused its military industry work on providing production materials and increasing production and repairs in the territory of Republika Srpska." It goes on to say: "Assets that could not be produced or repaired in the republic were purchased according to the needs of the VRS and the ability to fund the army's requests." What follows is a chart. General, can you explain for us the entries under number 1, which I suppose are typical of the chart? What can we read in row 1?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under 1, we have rifle ammunition. The amount produced and repaired in Republika Srpska, 864.000 bullets, that is to say; the amount purchased and donated, 61.590.737 rounds of ammunition; and finally, the sum total.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where it says "purchased," where was the rifle ammunition purchased, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, it was purchased in the special-purpose industry companies present in Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 7.62 rifle ammunition specifically, where was it produced?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the special-purpose industry company Prvi Partizan in Uzice.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The sentence below reads: "According to the plan of supplies for the VRS established by the state committee for procurements ..." Is that the committee you were referring to earlier on?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the reporting period during which the committee you've just referred to was active.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The sentence continues: "... 72 per cent of the level planned was indeed achieved."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you asked a question: "7.62 rifle ammunition specifically, where was it produced?" Which one is it under these? I've got this page 1 that goes up to item 9, I don't see any 7.62 ammunition there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Unlike the document we looked at yesterday, the ammunition has not been listed here by calibre, it only says "rifle ammunition." Still my question for the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My question to you is: If it is not mentioned by calibre here, how do you know that it's a 7.62-millimetre calibre? Why do you ask that question about the 7.62-millimetre calibre if it's not on the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because since I'm being asked this now, according to witness's testimony yesterday, 7.62-millimetre calibre was 99 per cent of the ammunition used. This is something that he said yesterday. Of course, it's not mentioned in the document here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are not asking what he said yesterday, you are asking him about this document. Some of us have had the fortune of not being military people, so we are not able to know these things unless we read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I put the question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm far from being knowledgeable in these matters. I myself have been learning throughout this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, this term here, "rifle ammunition," in your view what calibre does it refer to?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. Harmon, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think this calls for speculation. Unless this witness can give us precise information on this, he is speculating and I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are asking him in his view, sir. You know, look, you should --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will not ask him about his opinion. I'll ask him if he knows what this referred to, what the entry in row 1, what calibre it referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, the figure in column 1 of your report, do you know what calibre of ammunition it referred to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know full well that the VRS had as part of infantry weapons 7.62-millimetre automatic rifle Kalashnikov, and 7.62-millimetre semi-automatic rifle. With these two types of rifle --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object. Sorry, that's not responsive to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry? Sorry, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is not responsive to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the witness should first give a complete answer to my question, if he knows which calibre the ammunition listed under 1 here refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And this is my question for the time being, General. Can you answer that, the ammunition listed under 1, what calibre does it refer to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7.62 calibre for automatic rifle --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, with all due respect, unless the witness has such a photogenic memory and unless he himself in fact drew this, you are really calling for speculation. It doesn't matter how you ask the question. And I do -- I'm not quite sure how important it is for your case to establish that this rifle ammunition is a 7.62-millimetre calibre ammunition. It is ammunition whatever calibre it is, you know. I don't think it is very important to your case, but you might be thinking differently, but I think you really are moving into the realm of speculation if you persist with that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do consider this to be important for my case. Secondly, if you look at all the remaining columns in this document -- perhaps we can ask the witness to leave the courtroom if you want me to pursue this? Based on the columns and the figures contained therein and based on witness's knowledge dating from the period, I'm sure that he can give precise answers in relation to all the columns in this document when it comes to the calibre involved. He has first-hand knowledge of this, of the information listed in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that and you, yourself, have told us already that the witness told us yesterday that 99 per cent of ammunition was 7.62-millimetre calibre. To the extent that you expect him to remember in minute detail what each little order or each little ammunition was, I really wonder. But, you know, you go ahead, and if Mr. Harmon objects, he will object. Go ahead and ask your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, please look at all the columns before you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have looked at them already and it's all clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Based on the information contained in the columns, can you tell us what calibre they involved in view of the textual representation?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Column number 1, what calibre does it relate to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7.62 millimetre for automatic and semi-automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Column 2?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other infantry ammunition relates to the ammunition for pistols, rifle launchers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Artillery ammunition, what calibres does it relate to?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will not pursue this line of questions further. I'll go back to my previous question to you. The report says that 72 per cent of what was planned wasn't achieved. This 72 per cent, does it relate to what the army sought within its request or does it relate to what the committee established was indeed necessary for the army?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it refers to the requests put forward by the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order for Their Honours to be able to follow, the question I put to the witness has to do with the sentence that is on the next page in English. It is right below the chart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right below the chart, I'm not quite sure what that means?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the first sentence beneath the table. Actually what you see on the page in English is the latter part of the table or chart, and there follows the sentence which my question referred to. Now, let's look at another part of this report entitled "Financing the Defence." And let's look at page 9 in B/C/S and page 18 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the chapter dealing with how the defence was financed. The first paragraph is self-explanatory. It speaks of the insufficiency of the budget, and then it says: "For this reason, additional funds were secured from the state reserves for fuel to be obtained from abroad, and this is the information contained in the report." Do you know if the Supreme Command also discussed the need to obtain additional foreign currency funds for financing the defence efforts?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know, and this was one of the subjects most frequently discussed at the meetings of the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us turn to the next page, where various budget allocations intended for the army are discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, on this page what does the acronym "VK" mean, Mr. Kovacevic? There is a paragraph that says: "For these reasons, additional foreign currency funds were provided by VK from the state foreign currency reserve for the procurement of fuel and imported ammunition, the details of which are the subject of this report." What does VK mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the customary acronym for the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the same page in the B/C/S, could we just move the document a little to the left. Thank you very much. And in the English it's the following page. As for the English could we pull it down slightly. Thank you. But we need the next page in English, not this one. Could we go into private session, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, I would like to have more information about Pretis. In the former SFRY how important a company was this, in terms of their production activity back then?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Pretis Holding was one of the largest companies throughout the former Yugoslavia. It comprised about 20 different factories with different production programmes. It also had several factories that were involved in military purpose production, for the most part ammunition and systems required to use that ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Chamber knows about the location of Pretis, but can you tell us something about the size of the compound in Vogosca specifically?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was their HQ and all of their administration was there, all the projects were piloted from there, all of their technology was dealt with there. The mainstay of their production and the production lines for artillery ammunition were also based there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the distance between Pretis and the front line, the lines held by the enemy?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Pretis straddled the confrontation line, the distance being no more than several hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked you about the overhaul centre in Hadzici. Where was the overhaul centre located in relation to the line held by the enemy?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Hadzici overhaul centre also straddled the confrontation line. The distance never exceeding 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've explained about how the system operated and we heard about the manager too. Nevertheless, I would like to use some documents to illustrate that, the relationship between the defence ministry and Pretis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a 65 ter document, Defence document, 00779D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Pretis continue to operate and produce artillery ammunition throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it continued production throughout the war with several brief interruptions due to shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we just pull this up slightly to see who signed the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. First of all, are you familiar with this document and what can you tell us about it? I'm talking about the format rather than the substance. The substance is there for all to see.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first set eyes on this document, I believe, when the Tribunal's investigator spoke to me, or perhaps it was when I talked to you. The document was signed by the ministry secretary, Dragan Kapetina, on my behalf. The fact is, I didn't sign this document and that can only imply one thing, I was not involved in formulating the substance of this document or indeed deciding who the document would be addressed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Other than that, do you perhaps know if the defence ministry normally was in the business of granting approval for this kind of commercial transaction such as the one here involving Pretis and other commercial companies? If not, who was in charge of granting that kind approval?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the ministry did grant approval for the purchase and import of certain components on Pretis's behalf, making sure it was able to make contracts with special-purpose production companies in the FRY, depending on the calibre of the ammunition or other component parts, as covered by the agreement between the RS defence ministry and Pretis factory itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document please be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D416. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document I'd like to show the witness is from the 65 ter list of the Defence, 00754D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a document of the VRS Main Staff, dated the 3rd of December, 1994, and signed by Ratko Mladic, which is on the next page. Have a look at the document, please. I'm specifically interested in your comments on paragraph 2. Tell me first, in keeping with the regulations, which state agency or body of the army was in a position to be informed at all times of the production and placement of products from the Pretis factory?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The funds that the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska agreed with the Pretis factory should be used for purchases from them made it an obligation on the Pretis factory to inform the Ministry of Defence at all times of the amount of products produced, and they had to keep informed the Main Staff of these matters, as did the Ministry of Defence, which had to inform the Main Staff of the state of affairs with regard to ammunition and the distribution of ammunition. This was standard procedure. Everyone else who commissioned, purchased, or otherwise obtained ammunition from Pretis did not need to report on this to anyone, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we move into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at Defence Exhibit D53.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you go --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, yes, I wish to tender the previous document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 00754D is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D417. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, what do you want now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like us to look at a document, which is Defence Exhibit D53.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Look at the document, General, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the bottom of the document so that the General can see who signed it. Let's scroll up now so that the General can see the entire body of text.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's April 1995, Djordje Djukic addresses the Ministry of Defence and Pretis company on behalf of the Main Staff. I'm interested in what is stated under 1. Can you tell us what this is about and what was the purpose of this correspondence?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order for the Pretis company to be able to manufacture ammunition for the purposes of the VRS, the Main Staff decided to set aside for Pretis from its own reserves a certain amount of explosives. I think it's TNT. Now, the Ministry of Defence was requested to buy the explosives that were promised to Pretis in the special-purpose industry companies in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know in this instant case whether the extent mentioned in the document was indeed acted upon?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where were explosives produced in Yugoslavia, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the explosives and gun powder company Prva Iskra in Baric.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did this company have the same status as Prvi Partizan that we referred to yesterday? Is it a company from the special-purpose industry?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it applied to all the special-purpose industry companies present in the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have another question about Pretis. Do you know if the Army of Yugoslavia was interested in certain assets held by Pretis, and were there some talks about it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this case. I was personally involved in it. There was a specific production line machine in Pretis. It was a press, in fact. It was a very large machine. Now, the FRY Ministry of Defence wanted us to disassemble this machine and transport it to Yugoslavia. At the highest level in the country, at the level of the government, this request was denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, complete your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally called President Karadzic, President Krajisnik, the prime minister, the manager of the Pretis company, representatives of the SDS party, presidents of the municipalities of Vogosca and Rajlovac, as well as some other individuals, to attend a meeting which I chaired. At this meeting I lobbied for the machine to be disassembled and transported to Yugoslavia, and the reasons I put forward for it were that the machine was a very precious and expensive, one of a kind in the Balkans, that it would really be a pity if it were to be damaged by combat activities. However, they categorically rejected my proposal and this was something that I had to pay the price for in my subsequent career.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will move on to a different topic now. Did the military judiciary operate in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it had been set up and it was operational, but I have to tell you that I am not that familiar with that particular field.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know if within the VRS there existed and operated military disciplinary courts?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they had been set up. I know that they operated but I don't know to what extent they were indeed efficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time you were a member of the VRS and, later on, of the defence ministry, did you know that somebody from the Army of Yugoslavia could actually initiate disciplinary proceedings against you for something that you may have done within the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, sir. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, the witness is answering the questions very quickly, which makes my objecting very difficult because the answer is given as I stand on my feet. This witness is being asked a series of questions about the military judiciary and he has testified he is not familiar with that particular field, that was the answer he has given. So unless there is a proper foundation laid to asking questions where my colleague is going, I'm going to object and I'm going to object to this last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, yes, you are right that the witness said he didn't know just how efficiently the military judiciary operated, but I do not think that the question that was put to him is a question that he may not necessarily have knowledge about. He might know it, he might not know it, and I really don't think it's -- it doesn't go to the operation of the judiciary. It goes to whether somebody from the Yugoslav could initiate. If he knows, he knows; if he doesn't, he doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'll withdraw my objection to this particular question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, can you answer the question, or should I repeat it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time you were a member of the VRS and minister of defence, did you know that someone in the Army of Yugoslavia could, against you as a member of the VRS, initiate disciplinary proceedings for actions taken in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that disciplinary procedure for any breach of discipline had to be dealt with by a military court of Republika Srpska under the prevailing rules and regulations. I had never heard of a procedure where the Army of Yugoslavia would have jurisdiction or the VJ courts would have jurisdiction in relation to any breaches of discipline committed in the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I see that we are two minutes away from the break and I would like to move on to a different topic. Perhaps now would be the time to take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, was the defence ministry in any sense involved in regulating the service status in relation to certain ranks, specifically the defence minister? If so, which?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was, under the Law on the Army and the law on the -- rather, the defence ministry was in charge of appointments, defining establishment posts, and promotions of officers to the rank of colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the the Supreme Command ever discuss promotions or appointments for certain officers? Was that ever raised at any of these meetings?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our next document, it's part of the personal file which did not become a P exhibit in relation to Mr. Kovacevic, nevertheless it is on the OTP 65 ter list, 07841. Page 129 in the B/C/S. And the ERN for the English is 0611-5816-ET.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is this a Defence document, is it 07841D, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I just called it up as a 65 ter document, OTP. The personal file from the OTP 65 ter list, we've got that in our 65 ter list as well but this is how I've called it up. I think it might be easier to find like this. I just want to look at this one page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the decree on my promotion to the rank of major-general, signed by the president of Republika Srpska, Dr. Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are promoted to the rank of major-general in which army?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in charge of promotions and appointments of generals in the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday or two days ago, you told us when you were appointed defence minister. You said that the position had something to do with the rank. Does the date tally with the time of your appointment as defence minister?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there is a discrepancy in terms of the actual dates because that one said the 19th of January, 1993, as far as I remember, and it should be easy enough to check; whereas here it says promoted as of the 1st of February, 1993, or promotion to take effect on the 1st of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You see the date in the header for this decision?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the decree bears the date of the 19th of January. I do apologise, it does appear to be consistent. What I said a while ago was because I had not paid sufficient attention to the date stated here. The 19th of January is the right date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacevic, just correct me, did you not say at the beginning of your testimony that when you were appointed minister, you were promoted to colonel-general?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I don't think I said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a number for this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm advised that it is already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, at one point in time did you receive the rank of major-general in the VJ?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was at one of the Supreme Command meetings. General Mladic informed me that my promotion to the rank of general had been approved by the Supreme Defence Council of the FRY, approved and ratified, because all of the legal conditions had been met.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When one is given the rank of general, does that affect one's salary?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. The salary is higher than that which pertains to lower ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when exactly you got a pay rise, in relation to this date, when Karadzic promoted you or later on when Mladic informed you about the decree in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The pay rise came after my promotion was ratified in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you served this decree, a copy of this decree promoting you to the rank of major-general in the VJ?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. Nor indeed have I ever seen a copy of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's move on to an entirely different topic. What can you tell us about the Contact Group plan and the view of the political and military leaders of the RS regarding that plan on a peaceful solution to the crisis in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the leaders of the RS, at least to the extent that this was debated at Supreme Command meetings, and President Karadzic were committed to finding a way out of the existing crisis by peaceful means. They were committed to putting a stop to the war. The Contact Group was to try and understand the position of Bosnian Serbs. They were not to be forced into a position where they would be vanquished or crushed in any of the enclaves. Rather, they should remain within the framework of Bosnia-Herzegovina as internationally recognised country, nevertheless as a separate entity which in territorial terms would have links it to the territory of the then-FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you attend any of the Supreme Command meetings at which this was debated, the solution proposed by the Contact Group?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did attend some meetings where that was discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am afraid we'll have to move into private session now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to seek the Chamber's approval now for me to look at something from Ratko Mladic's documents with this witness. For familiar reasons it was not in our previous 65 ter list. This 65 ter 03378D. That's the Defence list. This is from folder 31, for the benefits of my friends from the OTP. The Supreme Command meeting dated the 14th of July, 1994. I would like to seek the Chamber's approval to orally introduce this document to our list and then comment on a number of things with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's about to appear on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 14th of July, 1994, Supreme Command meeting of the RS. We see the agenda there as stated: "1. Discussion of the implications of accepting or rejecting the Contact Group plan. "2. Supplying the army. "3. Personnel issues." General, there's one thing I would like to ask you to do. We cannot tell who attended the meeting and your name is not among those who contributed. Nevertheless, during proofing I had you read this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go to page 2 for a moment and then we'll be going back to page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page 2 -- then we are about to look at the English too. "General Mladic: Reject the plan, win the war." In capital letters. During proofing I read this back to you. Did that jog your memory in any way? Were you there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm looking at this utterance by General Mladic: "Reject the plan, win the war." I fully remember hearing these words at the Supreme Command meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please go back to the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And may I have you comment, please, on the following, what it says under number 1: "Karadzic, item 1." And then in parentheses it says: "(Speaking spontaneously, as usual)" or extemporising as usual, "and then 48 per cent is being offered and it is believed that we will get 1 per cent in Sarajevo. We told Herd yesterday that 49 to 51 was a one-day offer from the Serbs and the Croats."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see a discrepancy with the English there. It reads: "We told Hertz."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Herd was at the time?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember Herd.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Douglas Herd, doesn't that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name does ring a bell but I can't remember his specific role in these talks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Karadzic is quoted there as saying something. Does that jog your memory? What he is telling the Supreme Command here?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. There is was this permanent offer that Mr. Karadzic was telling the Supreme Command about as well as the government in parliament. It's entirely consistent with my memory of how things happened at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just wanted to find out from Mr. Kovacevic if he remembers what a "one-day offer" means in context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It means the offer has been on the table a long time because it's on the table every day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, can you comment on the following sentence, it's right underneath. Please look at that: "The impression is that he is hesitant and inclined more to accept than to reject." And then next to that we see "RM" and then under lined, the two letters. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you explain what that means?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fully agree. My impression was always, based on my knowledge of such information, that President Karadzic was more inclined to accept and less inclined to refuse. The remark is consistent with my own view. "RM" stands for "Ratko Mladic," that means he wrote that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this take you back to the meeting? Did Ratko Mladic actually utter this in public, or is it an observation that he jotted down in this notebook? Also what it says in parentheses, "extemporising as usual"?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't actually voice this. He secretly or covertly made a note to himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please move on to page 3. There are some sections here that are quite self-explanatory. Page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We looked at the agenda a minute ago. Number 2 is supplying the army, number 3 is personnel issues. So again I'm looking at the words attributed to President Karadzic. It reads: "Some of the officers are behaving towards the SDS and the civilian authorities as if they were not theirs." Does that take you back, sir? Was this the position expressed by Karadzic at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. That was an ongoing problem and here it found this expression and was expressed by this assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next thing it reads: "3 per cent of the budget has gone to the army. It is a catastrophe. Had the entire GDP gone to the army, it would have been still very little." What exactly did Karadzic mean by that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was another problem between Karadzic and Mladic. It is quite true that Karadzic held this view; namely, the view that the army was asking too much and that no budget could cope with such demands.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The last sentence, again I see a discrepancy between the B/C/S and the English. I'll read it the way I see it and you correct me if I'm wrong, please. "250.000 dinars was in the HK," that's what I see, "for two and a half months." And the translation reads "KK." Can we agree that the abbreviation there is "HK" and what is that a reference to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm tell you what I know and what it actually says. 250.000 dinars remained for two and a half months in the Herzegovina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why would he say something like this at a Supreme Command meeting?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he personally used some extra budgetary funds - when I say "he," I mean Karadzic - to send funds to the Herzegovina Corps so they could make some purchases on their behalf. Nevertheless, they did not do that. And they did not use the funds. The funds had been unused for two and a half months by this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be exhibited and for the time being can it be placed under seal, and can we also go back into open session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number, kept under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D418, admitted under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, we have heard a great deal of evidence before this Chamber what the decision of the authorities of the RS was in relation to this Contact Group plan. We also heard what had happened between the FRY and Republika Srpska thereafter. Did you, yourself, feel any consequences flowing from the failure to accept the Contact Group plan, and if so, which ones?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The consequences were indeed heavy and negative for the entire government, and the authorities as a whole. I personally had great many problems, as did other leaders, and I mean Mladic, Karadzic, Biljana Plavsic, Koljevic, and several other ministers --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I'm going to object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The question was a very narrow question. It was whether he felt any consequences flowing from the failure to accept the the Contact Group plan, and now we are going into potentially consequences for other people.
