He has named Plavsic, Koljevic, Karadzic, et cetera. So it's not responsive to the question and I object on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the objection is premature. The witness is answering for himself and the fact that he is mentioning other individuals as well does not mean that he has gone beyond the scope of my question. I'm sure that he can explain why he has been referring to other individuals as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just so that we avoid objections. Can you ask him to stick to the consequences that he personally felt, like the question said; and if you want to know about consequences for other people, then you can put that question later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, please try and give answers that will focus on my questions and so your stay in The Hague will be much shorter. So you personally, which were the consequences you felt as a result of the rejection of the Contact Group plan?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was forfeited my salary. I was banned from physically entering into the FRY. My photograph, together with my particulars, was held by the staff at all the border crossings. It was a sort of a wanted list issued by the organs of the FRY. They were instructed that should I be seen at one of the border crossings, that I should be banned from entering the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Such were the measures implemented against me and the result was that I did not have any means of livelihood and I could not visit my family in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall how long the measures you've just described for us were in force?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the way through to the end of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For how long did you go without your salary?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think four or five months.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the measures of forfeiture of pay were applied to other individuals, and if so, which ones?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that all the officers who had their status settled in Yugoslavia were forfeited their pay. However, I was the only one who was banned from entering Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The ban of entry to Yugoslavia was it enforced in relation to any other individuals but for yourself and the ones that you said did not have that measure?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that my photograph had been distributed to all the border crossings with such instructions. I don't know about the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you asked that question, the witness said: "However, I was the only one who was banned from entering Yugoslavia." You asked exactly that question after he has given you that answer. And now he gives you a different answer, he says he doesn't know. Just before you asked, he said he knew that he was the only one. Now we are confused, we don't know which one to accept.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the witness is the best placed to explain this if we created this confusion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, the ban of entry, complete with the photograph and particulars, related to Karadzic, Krajisnik, Biljana Plavsic, Koljevic, and myself. And I was the only officer -- the only general of the VRS among them. That was why I said that I was the only one because I meant in relation to my membership of the army and my generalship. I was the only one who had that ban of entry that was present at all the border crossings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us proceed in chronological order, General. You told us when it was that you were replaced as defence minister. Can you tell us what was the information you had regarding the reasons for your removal, and did you know who was behind it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have this information, not any reliable information, until I was served the decree signed by the FRY president, Lilic. I turned to President Karadzic with the request for an explanation as to why I was being retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, pause there. We haven't got to that point yet. We want to cover the period between mid-1994 and mid-1995. I only wanted to know whether you knew why you were replaced as defence minister in the summer of 1994. Did you ever learn the reasons why and the individuals behind your removal?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. President Karadzic told me that the Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party had asked him to replace me as the defence minister because they did not trust me, and because I was not a yes man and did not obey the party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you clarify this little confusion in my mind. You first answered this question by saying you did not know until you were served with a decree signed by the FRY president, Lilic. Now you say you were advised by President Karadzic that the Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party asked that you be replaced because they did not trust you, because you were not a yes man. How come that -- first of all there are two things. You said you didn't know about this until you were served with a decree, which means you couldn't have heard it from Karadzic. Now, I don't know when Karadzic told you that the board said this, but more importantly, I don't know -- can you explain why you were being replaced by a decree issued by an FRY president?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I caused the confusion and I apologise truly. By your leave, the answer I gave to the last question put by Mr. Lukic is correct. I was replaced as defence minister for the reasons I stated and which originated from the executive committee of the Serbian Democratic Party. As for my retirement, my later retirement, that's where I can explain in the context of Mr. Lilic's decree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Once you were replaced as defence minister, you were appointed deputy defence minister, as we heard from you, and this -- you continued in this position until the summer of 1995. Did you continue to have contacts with Karadzic and Mladic in that new position of yours, and if so, what did this contact have to do with?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had contact with them but only at the meetings of the state committee for centralised procurement of goods for the armed forces of Republika Srpska. And possibly if they had any requests to make of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just explain something for me again. They didn't trust you as a minister but they trusted you as a deputy minister? Was that the situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They only trusted me insofar I was able to perform technical duties that nobody was trained or equipped to deal with at that point in time. They did not want to dispense with me fully, but they did place me in a position that was in the side-lines completely. And they used the professional technical services I could provide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You say that as a deputy minister you were used to do technical work, not political work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh. We learn every day. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now complete the picture you just touched upon, Judge Moloto.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who was appointed your successor, i.e., the new defence minister?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ninkovic was, who had previously been SDS president for the region of Doboj and deputy of the SDS in the National Assembly of Republika Srpska. Milan Ninkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was he an officer too, as were you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was a civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the next topic we will have to move into private session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again we are dealing with documents belonging to Mr. Mladic, but we will be dealing with a document that we got a year ago. I talked to Mr. Harmon and none of us are sure whether the confidentiality status was abolished in relation to this diary from Mr. Mladic, which I know was admitted into evidence through a bar motion. So for the time being we should remain in private session and once all these documents are declassified, we will apply for this to be public. This document is not on our list --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, do you confirm?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 65 ter Defence document 03375D. This is a meeting at the command post held on the 11th of March, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, we went through this during proofing. This is a lengthy entry and I only wish to dwell on a number of details. It says "Kovacevic," and then it says, "a job in Greece." To make it easier for the Trial Chamber to later analyse the document, can you just tell us briefly when this meeting took place, what it was about, and against what background the meeting was held?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once we are done with this page, could we please flip to the next page in both the B/C/S and the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is mention there of $2 million at the beginning of this document. Could you just explain what that means.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I informed General Mladic that one should expect about $2 million in terms of proceeds from the goods that were sold. That is what I had been told by President Karadzic. The payment was to be made to one of the accounts in Greece.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page 2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honours, you can see that, I'm reading directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It reads: "From Israel - they offer joint combat against extreme Islam. "- offer the training of our men in Greece at their expense. They offer us special weapons for 500 men - sniper rifles for free - they said it came to Bihac. I don't know whether it was given to Serbia." End of quote. General, this entry, what is it about, who is it about?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this. I made two visits it to the Greek prime minister, Mr. Papandreou. I also had a meeting with their foreign minister, Mr. Papoulias, and their defence minister as well. During one of these visits I was contacted by the Israeli intelligence service. They informed me about quite a large number of Mujahedin being dispatched to Bosnia-Herzegovina. They told me all about the channels along which this operated and all about who was bank-rolling the whole operation. They said the objective was to drive Serbs out of certain areas altogether, specifically Ozren and Doboj. They offered both weapons, a minor amount albeit, and to train our men for free, but this was only to apply to fighting the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, let me interrupt you, Mr. Kovacevic. In your answer you tell us how you met the Greek prime minister and the foreign minister and the defence minister, and that they offered to train your men for free. But the question that is put to you is about an entry that relates to Israel, not Greece. Look at the question that was put to you on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I had to answer like that. I was the one who was contacted. It wasn't something that happened at my request. It was the Israeli intelligence service who contacted me during my visit to Greece while I was visiting these ministers. I did not at any point in time say that anyone from Greece or indeed anyone from the Greek government made this offer. It was the Israeli intelligence service and their representatives alone. More specifically, the Mossad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that. But if you had said that in your answer that while you were in Greece you met Mossad people, rather than tell us about Papandreou and other people, because those are not the sources of your information. You confuse us. If you can please try to focus on the question and answer the question. You see now you're -- instead of answering where you get the information from, you are giving us the context, that you got the information while you were in Greece meeting these people, and that's not part of the answer. And you will go home sooner if you can do that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I truly apologise for my clumsiness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are not being clumsy, but it's in the manner of speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page, please, both the B/C/S and the English. The last entry on that page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, it reads, again your words, apparently: "Through a certain (Nikolas) we can export plane engines to Iraq and Libya - Iraq also asks for R/D spare parts for tanks. Libya owes them a lot." Can you please comment on that, what was that supposed to mean?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. There was a mediator, a wealthy Greek offered this kind of arrangement. He was entertaining business links to Libya and Iraq.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two pages further into the document, both the B/C/S and the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It reads: "I'm still a freelancer. The problem is, Radovan thinks that I'm working for you, and you think that I'm working for him. I can work a lot, quietly and peacefully." What did this entry mean, because you are quoted as saying that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was trying to let them know that I was under pressure from all these insinuations to the effect that I was working for someone, be it Karadzic or Mladic, which was in the way of my professional and technical commitment. My commitment was to get this job done. I was trying to let them know that I could achieve a lot on the quiet, but as long as no one was meddling with my work and as long as no one was insinuating that I was doing the work on for someone or on someone's behalf. This was a purely professional endeavour for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is one thing that I would like to repeat because of the English translation. The interpreters could give me a hand with that. I don't think the English translation is appropriate. Again, this one sentence: "The problem is that Radovan thinks that I'm working for you, and you think that I'm working for him. I can do or achieve or work a lot, quietly and peacefully." I think the context is much clearer now in relation to what the official translation says. With regard to that, we have the correction entered and may this please be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number and kept under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D419, admitted under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, I would like to move on to a different topic, and namely that of the relationship between Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina. Can you tell us first of all, had you heard of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the counsel repeat what sort of declaration it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, can you please repeat what declaration it was, Mr. Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Had you heard of the Prijedor declaration? Can you answer the question, General?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A session was held of the Republika Srpska National Assembly together with the deputies of the National Assembly of the Republic of Serbian Krajina in the town of Prijedor. At that point, a declaration was adopted which stated that a unified body of -- a single body of territory would be set up, a single system of defence, a single army which was supposed to be headed by General Ratko Mladic. A single government would be introduced and a number of other issues were addressed in other decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up 00772D, a document from the 65 ter list of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the Prijedor declaration about -- on the unification of the RSK and the RS. The date is the 31st of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we can look at paragraph 3, we could scroll down the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It reads: "The two Assemblies proclaim that Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina shall form a defensive alliance with the task of providing equal protection to the freedom and integrity of the two republics until a final political solution is reached."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will read out another paragraph which is on the following page, Your Honour. And I would like the witness's answer to address both. I'm interested in the penultimate paragraph, the 13th paragraph of the declaration. It's on the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 13 reads: "The Assemblies of Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina proclaim the determination of the Serbian people in these republics to unify their state. This unification will be postponed until the expiry of the UN plan for the protection of the Krajina." It's a document dating from October and I'm interested in the subsequent period where you held the position we heard of. Did there persist among the VRS and the political leadership of the RS to be committed to the substance of this declaration?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that there remained the desire for the unity and a unified system of defence for the two countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the position of the FRY leadership was in relation to the declaration and the commitments stated therein on the part of the RS and the RSK?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the FRY leadership wanted to prevent this. What I saw as the problem was particularly the unification of special-purpose industry companies. The governments of the RS and the RSK had charged me with producing a programme to that effect. However, the leadership in Belgrade explicitly forbade this. What I heard was that President Bjelosevic forbade this and this programme was, in fact, never implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When it came to the unification of the political leaderships of the RS and the RSK, did you know or hear of any other meetings or agreements as a follow-up to the Prijedor declaration?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard from President Karadzic, at the time of my term within the committee for centralised procurement, that he would personally see to it that a unification is achieved above all of the defence systems of both territories.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of the Drina plan?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear of the plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And I would like to stop here for today, and I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D420. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Once again, Mr. Kovacevic, I remind you that you may not talk to anybody about the case while you are still in recess until you are completely excused from testifying. We have to break up for today. We'll come back tomorrow at 9.00, same courtroom. Court adjourned to Courtroom II, 9.00 in the morning, tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of July, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

[Private session] [Confidentiality partially lifted by order of Trial Chamber]
